title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Cooperation and Assistance in the 1988 Tax, Financial, and Price Inspections
keywords_en: Guarantee; Embezzlement; Acceptance of bribes; Offering bribes
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Cooperating with and Assisting the 1988 Inspection of Taxes, Finances, and Prices

Fa (Ban) Fa [1988] No. 21

All local people's courts at various levels throughout the country, all military courts at various levels, all railway transport courts at various levels, and all maritime courts:

1. On September 25, the State Council issued a notice, deciding to launch a nationwide inspection of taxes, finances, and prices for 1988 starting from October this year. Conducting this inspection well is of great significance for governing the economic environment and rectifying the economic order. This is an important measure to implement the spirit of the Third Plenary Session of the Thirteenth Central Committee of the Party. While studying, comprehending, and implementing the spirit of the Central Committee's plenary session, courts at all levels shall also pay attention to understanding and mastering the guiding ideology, scope, and focus of this inspection as stipulated in the State Council notice, as well as the handling of several specific policy issues. They shall fully exercise their adjudicative functions, closely cooperate, and vigorously assist to ensure the smooth development of this inspection.

2. Currently, economic criminal activities in society are quite serious, yet the number of economic criminal cases received by courts has been decreasing year by year. The reasons are multifaceted. An important reason is that criminals have not been subjected to the due penalties. Therefore, it is urgently necessary to strengthen work in this area and severely punish serious economic criminals. Based on the situation of tax, financial, and price inspections in previous years, as this inspection deepens, some economic criminal cases that constitute crimes and should be subject to criminal liability by judicial organs according to law, such as embezzlement, misappropriation of public funds, bribery, tax evasion and refusal to pay taxes, and speculation and profiteering, will be uncovered. After such cases are prosecuted to the courts, they shall be dealt with seriously in strict accordance with the Criminal Law and the relevant provisions of the decisions and supplementary provisions of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress, and no leniency or tolerance shall be shown. In particular, for cases of "official profiteering" uncovered, where a crime is constituted, the criminal liability of the directly responsible supervisors and other directly responsible personnel shall be pursued according to law. Care shall be taken to prevent the situation of "substituting fines for criminal penalties," lax handling, and insufficient crackdown, while also paying attention to correctly distinguishing the boundary between crime and non-crime, seeking truth from facts, and clarifying and confirming the facts accurately.

3. To effectively ensure the smooth progress of this inspection, courts at all levels shall, in accordance with law, strictly crack down on and promptly handle those persons who, by means of violence, threats, or other methods, obstruct the performance of inspection duties by relevant department personnel from taxation, finance, and pricing authorities, and who violate the criminal law.

4. During the inspection period, courts at all levels shall promptly select major and typical cases uncovered during the inspection, and using case examples to explain the law, conduct legal publicity through sentencing rallies, news reports, or other means, so as to expand the effectiveness of case handling.

5. Courts at all levels shall, in accordance with the provisions of the State Council notice, conscientiously conduct self-inspections and accept inspections. Where disciplinary violations are discovered, they shall be dealt with seriously and corrected promptly, setting an example of abiding by financial discipline.

October 13, 1988
